name: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for FDCS

criteria.description: Presence of spindle to ovoid tumor cells arranged in fascicles or whorls with vesicular nuclei
Positive immunostaining for follicular dendritic cell markers CD21, CD23, and CD35
Exclusion of other spindle cell neoplasms such as sarcomas, carcinomas, and lymphomas
Presentation as a slow-growing painless mass, often in lymph nodes or extranodal sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive immunohistochemical staining for follicular dendritic cell markers and exclusion of other neoplasms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunophenotyping, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a slow-growing mass in cervical or axillary lymph nodes
Commonly involves head and neck soft tissues, tonsils, or intra-abdominal sites

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats)
common.notes: May be present but less frequent than in lymphomas
searchTerms: general symptoms like chills and weight loss
constitutional symptoms including sweating and fever

common.symptomName: Mild pain or tenderness at tumor site
searchTerms: mild pain or tenderness at tumor site

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to marrow involvement or chronic disease
Less common than in other lymphoid malignancies
Due to involvement of intra-abdominal lymph nodes or masses
If mediastinal or pulmonary involvement present

rare.notes: Due to rare CNS involvement or compression

laboratory: Mild anemia or cytopenias in advanced disease
Normal to mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: CT or MRI showing well-defined soft tissue masses in lymph nodes or extranodal sites
genetic: No consistent recurrent genetic mutations identified
Occasional chromosomal abnormalities reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing spindle cells with vesicular nuclei
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD21, CD23, CD35

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of follicular dendritic cell markers (CD21, CD23, CD35)
Negative for follicular dendritic cell markers
Absence of follicular dendritic cell immunophenotype
Different histological patterns and marker expression

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss and night sweats
Neurological symptoms indicating possible CNS involvement
